full_description:
Windows Desktop Document Authoring Application — DOCX & Metadata

I am looking for an experienced Windows desktop developer to build a lightweight document-authoring application for internal use by my company.

The application will allow our document makers to create DOCX documents from scratch and apply the company's designated document properties and metadata at the point of creation.

The intended workflow is:

Create document → enter/edit content → apply company document properties → save/export as DOCX

The purpose is to avoid creating a document in Microsoft Word first and then having to manually change the document properties afterwards.

Core Requirements

The application should:

Be a Windows desktop application.

Allow users to create documents from scratch.

Allow users to edit document content.

Save documents as Microsoft Word-compatible .docx files.

Allow previously created documents to be reopened and edited.

Apply the company's designated document properties and metadata when the document is created.

Operate locally on the computer.

The metadata/document properties may include:

Author

Company/Organisation

Title

Subject

Keywords

Comments

Creator/Application

Custom document properties where technically supported

I want the developer to clearly identify which properties can be controlled reliably.

Not Required

The application does not require:

User accounts

Login

Payments

AI

Cloud services

External APIs

Online databases

Admin dashboard

iPhone/iPad application

Android application

The priority is a simple, reliable and cost-effective Windows application.

Recommended Technology

I am open to the developer's recommendation, but I expect C#/.NET with a Windows desktop framework such as WPF or WinUI to be considered because the application is specifically intended for Windows and needs to work closely with DOCX/Office Open XML documents.

The developer should explain the recommended technology and why it is appropriate.

DOCX / Open XML Requirement

Experience with Microsoft Word document formats and Office Open XML is particularly important.

A key requirement is:

Can you demonstrate that a DOCX created by your application contains the specified company document properties when inspected in Microsoft Word and through the underlying Office Open XML package?

I want this demonstrated with a working prototype before committing to the complete application.

Estimated Development Time

For the initial MVP, I would expect the developer to provide a realistic estimate after reviewing the requirements.

My preference is to start with a small paid prototype demonstrating:

Creating a DOCX from the application.

Applying the required document properties.

Saving the DOCX.

Opening it in Microsoft Word.

Verifying the document properties.

Inspecting the underlying Office Open XML package.

After that prototype has been successfully demonstrated, the remaining application can be developed in milestones.

Budget / Cost

I am looking for the cheapest practical and reliable solution.

I am open to offers from experienced developers and would like developers to provide:

Cost for the initial prototype.

Cost for the complete MVP.

Estimated cost for any optional features.

Fixed-price milestone breakdown where possible.

I am not looking for unnecessary features or an over-engineered solution.

Developer Experience

I am specifically looking for a developer who has experience with:

Windows desktop applications

C#/.NET or another suitable Windows desktop technology

DOCX document creation/manipulation

Microsoft Office Open XML

Document properties and metadata

Software testing

Please provide examples of relevant previous work.

Source Code

The complete source code should be provided as part of the project deliverables.

The application should be developed using version control, and any third-party libraries or open-source components should be identified along with their applicable licences.

Proposal Requirements

Please tell me:

What technology would you use and why?

Have you built Windows desktop applications before?

What experience do you have with DOCX/Open XML and document metadata?

Please provide examples of relevant previous work.

What would you charge for the small working prototype?

What would you charge for the complete MVP?

What is your estimated development time?

How would you divide the project into milestones?

Can you demonstrate the metadata functionality before the full application is developed?

What technical limitations or risks do you see?

Please do not send a generic proposal. I want a developer who understands the specific DOCX/document-metadata requirement and can explain a practical, cost-effective way to build it.

Any technical limitations or risks you see.

Please do not send a generic proposal. I would like you to specifically address the DOCX/document-metadata requirements.

I run a small marketing studio working with medical spas in the US. I'm looking for someone experienced in building lapsed-client win-back campaigns inside clinic booking software.

STARTING THIS WEEK — MILESTONE 1 ($75)

A test sequence built in a free trial account, using my own phone number and email, so we can start now rather than waiting for my next clinic to sign. Milestone 2 releases when a client campaign goes live.

THE WORK, PER CAMPAIGN

Each client has several hundred former patients who haven't booked in over a year.

— Pull the lapsed-client list inside the clinic's own software (Boulevard, Zenoti, Mindbody, Vagaro, Aesthetic Record or PatientNow)
— Segment it by last treatment type — injectables, laser, skin/facials, body
— Build a three-message sequence: SMS + email on day one, one reminder three days later
— Set stop rules: anyone who replies, books or opts out drops out of the remaining messages immediately
— Schedule sends in batches of 150–200 a day, not all at once
— Test the full sequence end to end before it reaches a single patient
— Pull the results afterwards: sent, delivered, replies, appointments booked

— Contact my clients directly, in any channel

— Press send on anything without my written approval

These are medical businesses and the data is patient data. You would be added as a named user on the client's system with a restricted, marketing-level role, granted by the clinic itself — never using my login, and never with access to clinical records. You would work under a signed confidentiality agreement, and a business associate agreement where the clinic requires one.

— Demonstrable experience with at least one of the platforms above

What is the proper Texas-law procedure for removing an initial director named in the Certificate of Formation before the first organizational meeting?
May two of the three initial directors hold the organizational meeting, adopt bylaws containing a director-removal provision, and then use that newly adopted provision to vote to remove the third initial director?

full_description:
CaroomX — Multiplayer Carrom Game
Game Concept

I want to develop a modern, competitive and highly engaging online multiplayer Carrom game called CaroomX.

The game should provide a smooth and premium Carrom experience with 1v1, 2v2, AI Bots, private rooms, matchmaking, virtual coins, rewards, leaderboards and advertisements.

The main goal is to create a game that is easy for new players to understand but engaging enough to keep players coming back every day.

---

1. Game Modes

1v1 Multiplayer

- Real-time 1v1 Carrom.
- Random matchmaking.
- Private room with room code.
- Friend invitation.
- Real-player matchmaking should always be prioritized.

2v2 Multiplayer

A major feature of CaroomX should be real-time 2v2 Carrom.

- 4 players in one match.
- 2 players per team.
- Team members should be clearly identified.
- Automatic turn management.
- Team score/progress visible to both teammates.
- Invite friends to create a team.
- Random 2v2 matchmaking.
- Reconnect support if a player temporarily disconnects.
- Automatic bot replacement if required.

Possible combinations:

2 Real + 2 Real

2 Real + 1 Real + 1 Bot

1 Real + 1 Bot vs 1 Real + 1 Bot

1 Real + 1 Bot vs 2 Bots

---

2. AI Bot System

Bots are especially important during the initial launch when the player base is small.

Bot matchmaking logic

1. Search for a real player first.
2. Wait for a configurable period, e.g. 10–15 seconds.
3. If a suitable real player is unavailable, automatically introduce a bot.

Bot difficulty:

- Easy
- Medium
- Hard

Bots should make realistic mistakes and should not play perfectly every time.

Bots must support both 1v1 and 2v2.

The backend must identify whether a participant is a real player or AI bot.

Bot rewards should be configurable from the admin panel.

---

3. Virtual Coin Economy

CaroomX will have its own virtual in-game Coins.

Coins are imaginary game currency and have no direct cash value.

New Player

Every new player receives:

1,000 free Coins

Ways to earn Coins

- Winning matches
- Daily login rewards
- Daily missions
- Achievements
- Level-up rewards
- Rewarded advertisements
- Events
- Referral rewards

Ways to spend Coins

- Paid-entry matches
- Tournaments
- Cosmetic items
- Board themes
- Striker skins
- Special effects
- Other in-game features

---

4. Match Coin Economy

Suggested initial structure:

Match| Entry Fee
Casual 1v1| Free
Low 1v1| 100 Coins
Medium 1v1| 500 Coins
High 1v1| 1,000 Coins
Low 2v2| 200 Coins/player
Medium 2v2| 500 Coins/player
High 2v2| 1,000 Coins/player

These values must be configurable from the Admin Panel.

A small percentage of the total entry pool can be removed as a game economy sink.

Example:

4 players × 500 Coins = 2,000 Coins

10% game fee = 200 Coins

Winning team receives = 1,800 Coins

The two winning players receive 900 Coins each.

---

5. Advertisement System

Integrate a suitable mobile advertising SDK such as Google AdMob.

Ad types:

- Rewarded Ads
- Interstitial Ads
- Banner Ads where appropriate

Rewarded Ads

Players can voluntarily watch an advertisement to receive Coins.

Example:

Watch Ad → +50 Coins

Suggested maximum:

10 rewarded ads/day

The reward amount and daily limit must be configurable.

Ads should never unnecessarily interrupt active gameplay.

---

6. Leaderboard & Ranking

Include:

- Global leaderboard
- Weekly leaderboard
- Monthly leaderboard
- Friends leaderboard
- 1v1 statistics
- 2v2 statistics
- Wins/losses
- Player level/rank

Future seasonal rankings should be supported.

---

7. Friends & Social Features

Players should be able to:

- Add friends
- See online/offline status
- Invite friends
- Challenge friends to 1v1
- Invite friends to 2v2
- Create private rooms
- Join using room code
- Use quick chat/emojis during matches

---

8. Real-Time Multiplayer & Reconnection

The game must use a proper real-time multiplayer backend.

The server should manage:

- Matchmaking
- Rooms
- Turns
- Game state
- Player movements/shots
- Scores
- Match results
- Coin transactions
- Disconnect/reconnect
- Basic anti-cheat validation

Temporary network disconnections should not immediately cancel a match.

Players should have a configurable reconnect window.

---

9. Security & Anti-Cheat

Important game data must be validated server-side.

The client should NOT be trusted for:

- Coin balance
- Match results
- Scores
- Rewards
- Turns
- Game state

The system should prevent:

- Coin manipulation
- Fake wins
- Duplicate rewards
- Advertisement reward abuse
- Referral abuse
- Client-side cheating
- Fake match results

---

10. User Account & Profile

Login options:

- Google Login
- Guest Login
- Optional email/mobile authentication

Profile should show:

- Username
- Avatar
- Level
- Coins
- Total matches
- Wins
- Losses
- Win rate
- 1v1 statistics
- 2v2 statistics
- Ranking

---

11. Daily Rewards & Missions

Daily login reward system with increasing rewards throughout the week.

Example:

Day 1 → 100 Coins
Day 2 → 150 Coins
Day 3 → 200 Coins
Day 4 → 250 Coins
Day 5 → 300 Coins
Day 6 → 400 Coins
Day 7 → 750 Coins

Daily missions could include:

- Play 2 matches
- Win 1 match
- Play 5 matches
- Win 3 matches

All rewards and limits must be configurable.

---

12. Future Monetization

The architecture should support future monetization through:

- Advertisements
- In-app purchases
- Coin packages
- Premium cosmetics
- Striker skins
- Board themes
- Special effects
- Tournament/event entries

No real-money gambling or cash-out system is required.

---

13. Admin Panel

A web-based Admin Panel should allow the owner to manage:

Users

- View users
- Search users
- Ban/unban users
- View player statistics

Game

- Match statistics
- Online users
- Active matches
- 1v1/2v2 statistics
- Bot settings

Economy

- Starting Coins
- Entry fees
- Winning rewards
- Game fee percentage
- Daily rewards
- Mission rewards
- Ad rewards
- Daily ad limits

Content

- Events
- Leaderboards
- Announcements
- Rewards

The important economy settings should be changeable without publishing a new app version.

---

14. Performance Requirements

The game should work smoothly on low and mid-range Android devices.

Requirements:

- Smooth animations
- Responsive controls
- Low latency
- Low mobile data consumption
- Fast matchmaking
- Quick loading
- Stable multiplayer connection
- Optimized network communication

The backend architecture should be scalable for future growth.

---

15. Main Screens

The application should include:

1. Splash Screen
2. Login/Register
3. Home
4. Profile
5. 1v1
6. 2v2
7. Casual Mode
8. Create Room
9. Join Room
10. Friends
11. Leaderboard
12. Missions
13. Daily Rewards
14. Coin Wallet
15. Shop
16. Settings
17. Matchmaking
18. Game Screen
19. Match Result

---

16. UI/UX

The UI should feel modern, premium and game-focused, not like a basic Carrom board application.

The Carrom board should have:

- Smooth striker movement
- Realistic coin physics
- Clean animations
- Sound effects
- Haptic feedback where supported
- Attractive player avatars
- Team indicators in 2v2
- Match statistics
- Smooth transitions

The interface should be simple enough for first-time users.

---

17. Required Deliverables

The freelancer/development team must provide:

- Complete Android source code
- Backend source code
- Database
- Admin Panel
- UI/UX assets
- Production APK/AAB
- Server deployment
- Multiplayer implementation
- 1v1 system
- 2v2 system
- Bot/AI system
- Coin economy
- Advertisement integration
- Documentation
- Complete source-code ownership/handover

The code should be clean, modular and documented so another developer can maintain and expand the project later.

---

18. Future Scalability

The architecture should allow future addition of:

- Tournaments
- Clubs/teams
- Seasonal events
- Advanced ranking system
- More game modes
- Voice chat
- More cosmetic items
- iOS version
- Additional languages
- Advanced AI bots

---

Core Vision

CaroomX should feel like a complete online Carrom gaming platform rather than just a simple Carrom game.

The key priorities are:

Fast matchmaking + Real-time 1v1 + 2v2 + Smart Bots + Virtual Coin Economy + Rewards + Social Features + Smooth Gameplay + Secure Backend + Ads + Scalable Architecture.

full_description:
Seeking an experienced **QA Engineer with full-stack development capabilities** to manually test an entire SaaS web application, identify and investigate defects, implement approved fixes, and regression-test those fixes.

**Manual QA is the primary responsibility of this role.** You must personally walk through and use the deployed application in a real browser as a customer, business user, and Platform Admin/staff user would.

Automated tests, typechecks, builds, scripts, linting, and other code-level checks are welcome as additional safeguards, but **they do not replace hands-on manual testing of the deployed application.**

Full-Platform Testing Scope
You will manually test all available pages, modules, and critical workflows across:
**Public Website & Customer Experience**
* Marketing and informational pages
* Navigation, links, buttons, and forms
* Public booking/customer experience
* Service and provider selection
* Availability and scheduling
* Customer information and confirmations
* Payments where applicable
* Booking changes and cancellations
* Validation and error states

**Entire Business Side**

* Registration and onboarding
* Authentication and account recovery
* Dashboard
* Appointments, calendar, and scheduling
* Clients/customers
* Services
* Team/providers and availability
* Payments and refunds
* Free trials, subscriptions, billing, plan changes, and cancellations
* Reports/analytics
* Account management and settings
* Roles and permissions
* Emails and notifications
* Other available business functionality

**Entire Platform Admin / Staff Side**

* Admin/staff authentication
* Admin dashboard
* Business and account administration
* User management
* Support functionality
* Administrative tools and workflows
* Roles and permissions
* Protected functionality
* Platform-level settings/actions
* Other available Platform Admin/staff functionality

The **entire business side and entire Platform Admin/staff side are required parts of the testing scope.**

Manual QA Requirements
Testing must involve real end-to-end use of the application, not simply confirming that pages load.
You will be expected to:
* Navigate through all major areas of the application
* Test buttons, links, menus, tabs, forms, modals, and other interactive elements
* Create, edit, and delete QA/test data
* Complete critical workflows from beginning to end
* Test valid and invalid inputs
* Test validation, empty, loading, success, and error states
* Verify data and session persistence
* Test authentication, protected routes, roles, and permissions
* Test unauthorized-access scenarios where appropriate
* Test interactions between customer, business, and admin workflows where applicable
* Test desktop and mobile/responsive behavior
* Test major supported browsers
* Perform exploratory and edge-case testing
* Identify functional, data, permission, workflow, and significant usability problems

You should actively look for issues that may not already be known.

QA Documentation & Bug Reporting
Maintain a clear **QA test matrix/checklist** showing what was manually tested, including the area/workflow, user role, result (**PASS / FAIL / BLOCKED**), related issue when applicable, and retest status.
Each identified bug should include:
* Clear issue title and severity
* Area/user role affected
* Steps to reproduce
* Expected vs. actual behavior
* Screenshot or screen recording when useful
* Browser/device where relevant
* Technical findings/root cause when identified
* Fix and retest status

A general statement that “QA passed” or “everything looks good” is not sufficient. We need clear documentation of actual test coverage.

Full-Stack Debugging & Bug Fixing
You must also be capable of technically investigating the issues you discover.
This may include diagnosing problems involving:
* Frontend
* Backend/server
* Database/data
* Authentication
* Authorization/permissions
* APIs
* Third-party integrations
* Environment/configuration
* Deployment/infrastructure

For **approved defects**, you will implement appropriate fixes, keep changes appropriately scoped, and avoid unrelated modifications.

Significant changes involving architecture, database schemas, security, billing logic, permissions, infrastructure, or core product behavior must be approved before implementation.

After a fix is available in the QA environment, you must **manually reproduce and retest the original workflow and check related functionality for regressions.**

GitHub & Development Workflow
**All code changes must be completed and delivered through our existing GitHub repository and established branch/deployment workflow. GitHub is the source of truth for the application code.**
You will be expected to:
* Work from the existing GitHub repository
* Use the designated QA/development branch
* Follow the established branch/deployment workflow
* Make clear, appropriately scoped commits
* Push completed work to GitHub
* Keep changes traceable and available for review
* Not create a replacement repository or separate codebase
* Not leave completed work only on a local machine
* Not make direct production changes outside the approved workflow

Manual testing should be performed against the appropriate **deployed QA/staging environment**, while approved code fixes should be made through the established GitHub workflow.

Production deployments and other high-impact changes require approval.

Qualifications
Looking for someone with experience in both **professional manual QA and full-stack web development**, including:
* Manual and exploratory SaaS testing
* Regression and end-to-end testing
* JavaScript/TypeScript
* React or similar frontend frameworks
* Backend/API development
* SQL/relational databases
* Authentication and authorization
* APIs and third-party integrations
* Git/GitHub
* Browser developer tools and network inspection
* Application logs and debugging
* Responsive web applications
* Deployment/configuration troubleshooting

Experience with **React, TypeScript, PostgreSQL/Supabase, Cloudflare, Stripe, Playwright, Cypress, or similar technologies** is a plus.

Deliverables
By completion of the engagement, we expect:
* Manual testing of the full provided platform
* Public/customer experience tested
* Entire business side tested
* Entire Platform Admin/staff side tested
* QA test matrix with PASS / FAIL / BLOCKED results
* Bugs documented with reproducible evidence
* Approved defects fixed through GitHub
* Fixes manually retested in the deployed QA environment
* Regression testing completed
* Critical end-to-end workflows verified
* Remaining known issues and blockers clearly documented

This is a **hands-on manual QA + full-stack debugging and bug-fixing role**. We need someone who will actually use the deployed product, find problems, investigate them technically, fix approved defects through GitHub, and manually verify that the application works afterward.
